newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian oil export staff strike off, pay agreed.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian oil export staff strike off, pay agreed.

text.p: Staff at Nigeria's Department of Petroleum Resources (DPR), which oversees crude oil exports, have shelved a plan to go on strike after government agreed to pay part of their outstanding salary, a union chief said on Monday.

"Our management told us this morning that it had received the cheque for January salaries and rent subsidies," Victor Ajakaye, chairman of the DPR chapter of the white-collar oil workers' union PENGASSAN told Reuters.
Union representatives from around the country arrived in Lagos at the weekend to decide on whether or not to go on strike to press for non-payment of their members salaries from January.
Ajakaye said the strike plan had now been shelved because DPR management said it had received the cheque for part of the salary arrears on Friday and was processing it.
"At least we now have something although we would have preferred to be paid the two months (January and February) salaries," he said.
Oil prices rose on Tuesday last week on news that the 3,000-strong DPR staff had threatened to go on strike if they were not paid by Friday.
The pay situation had heightened tension at several DPR locations.

Staff of the department have been disgruntled since last summer when the military government contracted outside inspectors to check oil shipments following allegations of overloading tankers to rob the government of oil revenues.
A strike by staff could disrupt Nigeria's oil exports since they carry out the documentation at export terminals.
